title: Multi-period Mean-Expectile Portfolio Optimization under Wasserstein Ambiguity: Reformulation, Degeneracy and the Role of the Ground Metric
summary: Expectiles are the only law-invariant risk measures that are both coherent and elicitable. Unlike Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR), however, they do not admit a Rockafellar--Uryasev representation that admits tractable Wasserstein reformulations. We address this difficulty by developing an envelope theorem for worst-case expectiles that characterizes the worst-case expectile over a Wasserstein ambiguity set as the unique root of a worst-case expectation with a two-piece affine integrand.
